# Spawn power-ups in combat base

## Goal

As a playtester, I want power-ups to drop in the enemy and boss gyms so I can observe drop cadence and placement under real enemy pressure.

User story: As a developer, I want the shared combat base scene to own an optional power-up layer so both `GymEnemies` (all archetypes) and `GymBoss` spawn drops without duplicating scene code.

## Scope

`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` plus enabling configuration in `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`. Collection and effects are handled by the follow-up item; this item covers spawning, cadence and placement only.

## Implementation notes

- Add an optional power-up configuration block to `EnemyFormationConfig` so a scene opts in; leave `GymPlayer`/non-combat consumers unaffected.
- Default ID selection uses `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9, seeded from the rules weights (`loadRules()`), with an injectable RNG for tests.
- Position each drop via the `PowerUpPlacement` strategy, passing live enemy positions (alive entities with their hit radii) and the player position.
- Maintain one drop on screen at a time; the next spawn occurs after the configured interval from the rules config.
- Enable the layer for `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss`, and expose read-only accessors so tests can assert cadence, drop IDs and positions.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria below.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` spawn one power-up at a time on the configured interval.
- [ ] AC2: The spawn ID is selected through a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 seeded from the rules weights) and is injectable for tests.
- [ ] AC3: The drop position comes from the pluggable placement strategy and never overlaps a live enemy body or the player.
- [ ] AC4: Scene-level tests verify the spawn cadence and the non-overlap guarantee for both combat gyms.
- [ ] AC5: Existing `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss` behaviour and tests remain green.
- [ ] AC6: `npm test` passes.
- [ ] AC7: Coverage reference (parent AC3): `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` spawn one power-up at a time on the configured interval, selecting the ID through a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights) and positioning it through the placement strategy; scene-level tests verify the spawn cadence and that spawned drops never overlap live enemies or the player.
data.title: Spawn power-ups in combat base

# Collect drops with effects and HUD

## Goal

As a playtester, I want to fly over a dropped power-up and observe its effect while dodging threats, so collection and effect behaviour can be validated in the combat gyms.

User story: As a developer, I want spawned drops to reuse the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and `EffectsRegistry`, rendered by the standalone HUD, in both combat gyms.

## Scope

`GymFormationScene` (shared by `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`) plus tests. Reuse existing implementations — do not fork `PowerUp`, `EffectsRegistry`, `HUD`, `icons` or `audio`.

## Implementation notes

- Give each drop the shared `PowerUp` grow → hold → shrink → despawn lifecycle and draw the icon via `drawPowerUpDrop`.
- Collection is fly-over: drop is collectible at ≥ 3 % scale and overlaps the ship hull; on collect apply through a shared `EffectsRegistry` and play the collect sound.
- Render the standalone `HUD` for active effects in both scenes (lives counter visible so P8 is observable).
- P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets without damaging enemies; P7 teleports via S/↓ to the nearest safe spot using the existing `findTeleportDestination` approach (extract to a shared helper if reused) granting P6 on arrival; P8 updates the lives counter; P9 stacks.
- Drive `effectsRegistry.tick(dt)` from the deterministic `tick(dt)` path and expose accessors for tests.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` (reuse)
- `src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (reuse)

**Acceptance Criteria below.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Spawned drops use the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap).
- [ ] AC2: Collecting a drop applies its effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry` in both scenes.
- [ ] AC3: Both combat gyms render the standalone HUD for active effects.
- [ ] AC4: P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets without damaging enemies; P7 teleport works via S/↓; P8 updates the lives counter; P9 stacks.
- [ ] AC5: Tests cover at least one collectible path per scene and each of the P4/P7/P8/P9 effects in a combat gym.
- [ ] AC6: `npm test` passes.
data.title: Collect drops with effects and HUD

# Live spawn-interval control

## Goal

As a developer, I want a live-tunable spawn-frequency control in the combat gyms so I can dial in the drop cadence without rebuilding.

User story: As a developer, I want a DOM-overlay slider (patterned on `GymPlayer`) that changes the running scene's spawn interval and persists it through the rules config.

## Scope

A shared control-panel helper plus wiring into `GymEnemies` (which already has a panel) and `GymBoss` (which needs one).

## Implementation notes

- Add a shared helper that builds a plain-DOM range input with a stable id and data attributes (assertable with `document.querySelector` in happy-dom), patterned on the `GymPlayer`/`GymEnemies` panels.
- On input, apply the new interval to the running scene immediately (next spawn uses it) and persist through `saveRules()`.
- Seed the slider from `loadRules()` and remove the panel on scene SHUTDOWN to avoid DOM leakage.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (or a new shared gym util)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`
- `src/core/rules.ts` (reuse)

**Acceptance Criteria below.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A spawn-interval slider is present in both `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`.
- [ ] AC2: Changing the slider applies the new interval to the running scene so the next spawn uses it.
- [ ] AC3: The value persists through the rules config and is restored from it on scene creation.
- [ ] AC4: A test covers live application and persistence.
- [ ] AC5: Panels are removed on scene SHUTDOWN.
- [ ] AC6: `npm test` passes.
- [ ] AC7: Coverage reference (parent AC6): a live spawn-interval control in the combat gyms changes the spawn cadence of the running scene and persists the value through the rules config; a test covers live application and persistence.
data.title: Live spawn-interval control

# Documentation for combat spawning

## Goal

As a developer, I want the repository documentation to describe the new configurable, weighted, pluggable power-up spawning in the combat gyms so future work has an accurate reference.

## Scope

Documentation and code comments only — no behaviour changes.

## Deliverables

- `./README.md` — document the combat gyms' power-up behaviour (weighted random ID selection, avoiding random placement, live spawn-interval control, collection + effects).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — note the configurable/pluggable spawning for the combat gyms (§4.4 power-ups, §6.4 gym scenes), including the relative-weight interpretation of the GDD rarity guidance.
- JSDoc/code comments on `src/core/rules.ts` and `src/powerups/placement.ts`.
- Remove or update stale references to the hard-coded spawn interval.

**Key Files:**

- `./README.md`
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `src/core/rules.ts`
- `src/powerups/placement.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria below.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `README.md` documents the combat gym power-up behaviour and the rules config.
- [ ] AC2: `docs/Game Design Document.md` records the configurable/pluggable spawning for `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`.
- [ ] AC3: `src/core/rules.ts` and `src/powerups/placement.ts` carry accurate JSDoc describing their behaviour.
- [ ] AC4: No stale references remain to a compile-time-only power-up spawn interval for the combat gyms.
- [ ] AC5: All written output uses UK English.
- [ ] AC6: Coverage reference (parent AC7): all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
data.title: Documentation for combat spawning
